questions.question: Explain the emerging trend of spiritual and pilgrimage tourism in India.

questions.question: Explain how empirical analysis can be used to understand tourist behaviour and / tourism trends.
questions.solution_html:
• Use of empirical analysis to understand tourist behaviour and tourism trends. (5
  • marks) Empirical analysis uses observed/measured evidence rather than assumptions (1)
  • Collect primary data: surveys, interviews, observation, focus groups; secondary data: arrival
  • statistics, booking records, reviews and reports (1) - Analyse expenditure, length of stay
  • purpose, satisfaction, origin and preferences using averages, percentages, comparisons or graphs
  • (1) - Compare groups, destinations or years to reveal patterns and changes (1) - Use findings for
  • planning, segmentation, product development, marketing and forecasting (1)
questions.final_answer: planning, segmentation, product development, marketing and forecasting

questions.question: Discuss the major challenges in analysing tourist behaviour and travel patterns.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Analyse the impact of digitalisation, social media, online travel agencies and / artificial intelligence on the progress of Indian tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of digitalisation, social media, OTAs and AI on the progress of Indian tourism.
  • ((15 marks)) Introduction: digital tools have changed how tourists search, compare, book
  • experience and review travel (1) - Digitalisation: websites, mobile apps, digital payments, e
  • tickets and online information improve access, convenience and efficiency (2) - Social media
  • images, videos, influencers, hashtags and user-generated content create destination awareness
  • and influence choices; reviews spread quickly (2) - Online travel agencies (OTAs): compare
  • prices/options, enable booking of flights, hotels and packages, widen market reach and support
  • small providers; commissions and platform dependence are challenges (2) - Artificial
  • intelligence: chatbots, personalised recommendations, demand forecasting, sentiment analysis
  • dynamic pricing and customer support (2) - Impact on Indian tourism: wider
  • domestic/international reach, easier trip planning, new business opportunities, better data-led
  • decisions and support for lesser-known destinations (2) - Challenges: digital divide
  • inaccurate/fake information, privacy and cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, platform costs and
  • reduced human interaction (2) - Conclusion: combine technology with reliable information
  • digital skills, inclusive access and responsible/sustainable destination management (2)
questions.final_answer: digital skills, inclusive access and responsible/sustainable destination management
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain measures of central tendency and discuss their applications in tourism / data analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Measures of central tendency and their applications in tourism data analysis. (15
  • marks) Introduction/meaning: central tendency summarises a dataset using a representative
  • central value (1) - Mean: sum of all observations divided by number of observations; explain
  • formula or calculation (3) - Median: middle value after arranging data; for an even number
  • average the two middle values; useful for skewed data/outliers (3) - Mode: most frequently
  • occurring value; useful for common package price, stay duration or visitor preference categories
  • where applicable (2) - Tourism applications: average tourist expenditure, length of stay, daily
  • spending, room rate, visitor numbers or satisfaction scores (2) - Interpretation/use: compare
  • destinations, seasons and visitor segments; support pricing, budgeting, marketing and planning
  • (2) - Limitations: mean is affected by extreme values; median ignores many individual values;
  • mode may be absent/multiple; measures alone do not show variation or explain causes (2)
questions.final_answer: mode may be absent/multiple; measures alone do not show variation or explain causes
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how tourist feedback, online reviews and social media data can be used / to identify emerging local tourism experience trends.
questions.solution_html:
• Using tourist feedback, online reviews and social media data to identify emerging local
  • tourism experience trends. ((15 marks)) Introduction: online and direct feedback provide
  • evidence of visitor needs, perceptions and changing interests (1) - Sources: questionnaires
  • interviews, review platforms, ratings, comments, hashtags, posts, photos, videos and
  • search/booking data (2) - Collection and preparation: define destination/time period, gather
  • relevant data, remove duplicates/spam where possible, protect privacy and organise themes (2)
  • Methods: review coding, frequency counts, ratings, sentiment analysis, keyword/hashtag
  • analysis, observation and comparison over time (3) - Identify trends: local food, culture and
  • crafts, community-led activities, nature/adventure, wellness, authentic experiences or less
  • crowded places, where supported by the data (2) - Interpretation: compare seasons, visitor
  • segments and positive/negative feedback; triangulate online data with surveys, observation and
  • stakeholder views (2) - Applications: improve products and service quality, support local
  • businesses, target marketing, manage visitor flows and guide sustainable planning (2)
  • Limitations/conclusion: online users may not represent all tourists; fake reviews, language, bias
  • and changing platforms affect reliability; use ethical, balanced and regularly updated analysis (1)
questions.final_answer: and changing platforms affect reliability; use ethical, balanced and regularly updated analysis
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
